title: Topos Institute Research Bridge

hero.headline: Which structure survives the translation?
hero.support: Boundary First Labs is developing Schemathematics and related representational machinery under a strict reduction rule: import mature formalism where it is sufficient, expose the residual defect where it is not, and do not mistake new vocabulary for new mathematics.

bflSide: Schemathematics as an operational study of formal structures across schemas.
Representational Mechanics as the study of preservation, distortion, transport, and repair across representations.
Admissibility constraints governing what may be introduced, forgotten, compressed, or reconstructed.
Categorical/compositional computation as an open research direction rather than an established contribution.
sharedResearchSurface: Finding the right abstraction for systems whose local representations must compose.
The relationship between formal equivalence and operational asymmetry.
Whether Boundary First constructs reduce cleanly to existing categorical systems theory, applied category theory, type-theoretic, or formal-methods machinery.

candidateExperiment.title: Reduction before invention
steps: Select one Schemathematics object or Boundary First invariant contract.
Represent it using the strongest relevant established categorical machinery.
Measure whether any claimed residual defect remains after the translation.
Retire the Boundary First primitive if the mature formalism already carries the necessary structure.
candidateExperiment.successCondition: A useful result includes clean reduction. The collaboration is successful if it tells us what not to invent.

firstAsk: Try to reduce the proposed machinery to established category-theoretic or compositional systems language and identify the smallest residue, if any, that survives.
claimBoundary: This page does not imply Topos Institute endorsement, partnership, affiliation, or review.
Schemathematics is a research program with an active novelty burden, not a declared replacement for category theory or existing formal methods.
Categorical Turing Machines and related compositional computation work remain open research directions.
Any claim of novelty must follow documented attempted reduction against established mathematics.
notes: Use as an unlisted direct-outreach page only.
